catalog_quote: 22.2 Syllable length and rhythmic patterning. Syllable length is important in Macushi for the way it influences rhythmic patterning. ... The basic rhythmic pattern of a sequence of V or CV syllables within a word/phrase is short-long-short-long, etc. (where "long" is defined as having stress and vowel length). The final CV in a phonological phrase (i.e., a phrase bounded by pause) is always long and stressed, but within the phrase, even across grammatical word boundaries, the pattern is that the even numbered V or CV syllable, counting from the left, is long: (1) arimarakayamî (V.CV̄.CV.CV̄.CV.CV̄.CV̄) 'dogs' ... [p.146] (ii) Syllables that contain a contrastively long vowel (sect. 22.1.2) or a diphthong, i.e., CVV syllables, and VC and CVC syllables, are inherently long and affect the basic pattern accordingly. Thus: eipepî (V̄V̄. CV. CV̄) 'I am ashamed.' eerepamî (V̄V̄. CV. CV̄. CV̄) …
